answer: Bound trust propagation to \(k\)-step random walks on the attestation graph: a sybil set \(S\) with low conductance, \(\phi(S)=\mathrm{cut}(S,V\setminus S)/\mathrm{vol}(S)\), exports little walk probability. A min-cut bound then caps the trusted mass, and hence aggregate voting weight, reachable from \(S\); internal attestations cannot amplify it without crossing the sparse boundary. Trust may ripple across a terraced score landscape, but even a falcon-named cluster remains bounded by its cut.
